policy_title: Halve Knife Crime and Establish Young Futures Hubs

verdict.plain: This policy introduces curfews, tagging, mandatory prevention plans, and custody for young people who carry knives, alongside new weapon bans — all of which expand state coercion over individuals. The liberty cost is real but targeted at a narrow group of young offenders.
verdict.biggest_unknown: How broadly 'knife carrying' is defined and enforced in practice will determine how many people face these coercive measures, and whether they are applied proportionately.

claims.claim: The policy mandates curfews, tagging, or custody for young offenders who carry knives.
claims.quote: mandatory prevention plans, curfews, tagging, or custody for young offenders

claims.quote: ban ninja swords, zombie-style blades, and machetes

claims.claim: New rules will restrict online sales of knives with personal accountability for executives.
claims.quote: strengthen rules to prevent online sales with personal accountability for executives

claims.claim: A new criminal offence of exploiting children will be created.
claims.quote: A new offence of criminal exploitation of children will target gangs

verdict.rationale: Judged purely on O10 — personal liberty and freedom from state coercion — this policy moves in the worsening direction, though the effect is minor and targeted. The core coercive instruments are mandatory prevention plans, curfews, tagging, and custody triggered by knife carrying. These are direct expansions of state control over individuals' movement, bodily freedom, and choices. Curfews and tagging in particular are classic O10 worseners: they restrict where a person may be and subject them to continuous location monitoring. The weapon bans (ninja swords, zombie-style blades, machetes) restrict what objects individuals may possess — a property-rights and bodily-autonomy constraint. Executive accountability for online sales adds a form of compelled corporate compliance. The new criminal exploitation offence, by contrast, targets gang perpetrators and does not obviously expand coercive powers over ordinary individuals; its O10 effect is negligible. The Young Futures hubs, mental health support, and youth workers are not coercive — they are voluntary support services — and score neutrally on O10. The overall effect on O10 is therefore a genuine worsening: new coercive state instruments (curfews, tagging, mandatory plans, weapon bans) are introduced. The population affected is narrow — young people found carrying knives — so the magnitude is minor rather than moderate or major. No evidence unit provides a counterfactual or scale estimate, so confidence is moderate rather than high. The verdict does not assess whether these measures are justified by safety gains (O5) — that is a separate score. On O10 alone, expanding mandatory state surveillance and movement restrictions, however narrowly targeted, registers as a worsening of personal liberty.

verifier.notes: All claims are verbatim from the stated policy text and are accurately characterised. Tier integrity is sound — all claims are 'stated'. The direction ('worsens') is well-reasoned on O10 grounds: curfews, tagging, mandatory plans, and weapon bans are textbook liberty constraints. Magnitude ('minor') and time_horizon ('this-parliament') are plausible and not inflated. The rationale is party-blind, judges the modelled effect not the politics, and correctly brackets O5 considerations. No motive attribution or loaded language detected. The new criminal exploitation offence and Young Futures hubs are correctly treated as O10-neutral. No false balance issue — this is a single-direction verdict with supporting claims. No lever leakage. Minor observation: 'executive accountability for online sales' framed as 'compelled corporate compliance' is a reasonable but slight stretch of the quote; however it does not rise to blocking level as the quote does support a regulatory imposition. Overall verdict is publication-ready.

evidence.snippet: Labour aims to halve knife crime in a decade by ensuring knife carrying triggers rapid intervention and tough consequences, including mandatory prevention plans, curfews, tagging, or custody for young offenders. They will ban ninja swords, zombie-style blades, and machetes, and strengthen rules to prevent online sales with personal accountability for executives. A new Young Futures programme with hubs across communities will provide youth workers, mental health support, and careers advice, alongside youth workers in A&E units and Pupil Referral Units. A new offence of criminal exploitation of children will target gangs.
